title: Decision lattice for small-sample A/B and staged graceful-degrade for Optimize
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD to define a decision lattice and operational acceptance contract for Optimize evaluations when sample sizes are small or traffic is heterogeneous. Goal: provide deterministic, auditable rules for accepting or rejecting model/quantization/promptset changes during staged rollouts that balance sensitivity to regressions with tolerance for expected variance in low-traffic cohorts. This covers prompt cohort sampling, statistical test selection, traffic shaping for canaries, time-windowed decisioning, acceptable false-positive/false-negative trade-offs, and automated/manual rollback handoffs.
scope: Define minimum sample sizes and progressive thresholds for cohort-level A/B comparisons
Specify statistical tests and stopping rules appropriate for low-n cohorts (including sequential methods)
Prescribe signal weighting across latency, correctness, and domain-specific quality metrics
Define automated rollback triggers and recommended manual escalation paths
Provide a rollout recipe (shadow -> canary -> ramp) with guardrail timings and observability requirements
Deliver sample dashboards and alert semantics that product/DS/eng can consume
out_of_scope: Model training changes or retraining cadence policies
Deep instrumentation changes to runtime kernels (those are separate infra projects)
acceptance_criteria: Decision lattice is documented and reviewed by Eng, DS, and SRE
For canaries with expected daily requests < 500, a sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) or Bayesian sequential test is available in the eval harness
Automated rollback rules implemented in the rollout service: high-severity rollback within 5 minutes of trigger, degradations of medium severity queued for human review within 2 hours
Dashboard exposes per-cohort delta, p-value/posterior probability, cohort n, and a computed risk score within 15 minutes of data arrival
A/B jobs default to a conservative decision window (72 hours) for small cohorts but allow configurable fast-fail paths for high-severity regressions
Playbook with step-by-step operator actions and runbook links is attached and validated in a dry-run exercise
success_metrics: False-positive rollback rate <= 3% over first 90 days across all canaries
Average time-to-rollback for P1-quality regressions <= 6 minutes (measured from trigger to traffic divert completion)
Reduction in unplanned production degradations attributable to Optimize rollouts by 40% within first quarter after launch
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Offline evaluation using historical prompt cohorts and synthetic noise injection
Stage 1: Shadow traffic for 48h across representative cohorts (no user-visible change)
Stage 2: Canary at 1% traffic in 2 cohorts for 72h with sequential tests enabled
Stage 3: Progressive ramp (1% -> 5% -> 25%) only if no severe trigger within decision windows
Stage 4: Full rollout with continued monitoring and automatic rollback disabled (manual oversight) for first 7 days
test_plan: Offline: run cohortized A/B with injected regressions to validate detection sensitivity and false alarm rates
Pre-launch: dry-run of rollback pipeline using a synthetic trigger (alerts generated but no traffic diverted) to validate operator flow
Canary: real traffic canary with controlled seed and explicit guardrails; verify dashboard and alerting are green
Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring sweep with automated report and incident retrospective if any rollback occurred
statistical_tests: Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) for binary correctness signals
Bayesian sequential testing (posterior probability thresholds) for model-quality metrics with continuous scores
Nonparametric Mann-Whitney U for small-n ordinal signal comparisons where distributional assumptions fail
Bootstrap-based confidence intervals for latency and skewed metrics
rollback_triggers: P1 trigger: any cohort shows > 15% increase in critical failure rate with posterior probability >= 97% (auto-rollback)
P2 trigger: cohort shows 10-15% degradation on primary quality metric with p-value < 0.01 over 24h (auto-notify + 2h human window)
Latent-degradation trigger: median latency regressions > 2x baseline for 95th-percentile requests for 30 minutes (auto-failover to previous model variant)
Composite-signal trigger: concurrent small deltas across three independent signals (quality, hallucination, latency) that produce a computed risk score >= 0.85 (requires human review)
Traffic-threshold safety: if cohort n < minimum_sample_size for SPRT, default to hold traffic and extend decision window rather than forced rollback
minimum_sample_size_note: Default minimum sample size per cohort = 250 requests for binary signals; for continuous metrics rely on sequential tests but require at least 100 observations before any auto-rollback decision
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: small cohorts produce noisy signals -> Mitigation: use sequential tests and aggregate across related cohorts with a hierarchical prior
Risk: delayed instrumentation can mask fast degradations -> Mitigation: require end-to-end latency instrumentation and synthetic heartbeats during canaries
Risk: too-aggressive auto-rollbacks cause churn -> Mitigation: conservative auto-rollback thresholds and automated fallback to a stable variant rather than full disable
Risk: operator overload and alert fatigue -> Mitigation: tier alerts by severity and provide a summarized daily digest for low-severity anomalies
